newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Travel up after share placement.
newsitem.headline: China Travel up after share placement.

text.p: Shares of China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd rose on Tuesday after the company announced a share placement to raise capital to fund asset acquisitions, brokers said.
The company's shares, which topped the most active list by turnover, were up HK$0.05 at HK$3.835 in mid-morning on volume of 53.6 million shares worth HK$203.91 million.
"The market has been reasonably positive on red chips that can issue shares, raise money and then inject good assets into it," said Gilbert Chu, head of research at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"So I think people are going to receive positively the China Travel placement -- not as an EPS (earnings per share) diluting one but rather an EPS enhancing one," Chu added.

China Travel said on Tuesday its majority shareholder China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd would sell 420 million existing shares to institutional investors at HK$3.60 each and subscribe to 700 million new shares at the same price.

The company said the net proceeds of about HK$2.5 billion after expenses would be used for investment projects and purchase of assets, including toll roads, hotels and investments in passenger transportation and freight forwarding businesses.
"I think all kinds of red chips could see a correction in the short term," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at ImPac Asset Management.

"After the recent rally I think the stocks will have to consolidate and let investors think about which ones will be quality stocks. I still believe they will remain the focus this year but I think they really have to take time to consolidate," Tang said.
